sections.label: The opening
sections.line: How to think about offers to license a book that started on Leanpub, and what to keep.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: A publisher asked; others take such books; Leanpub leaves rights with the author; the questions are about scope.

sections.label: The approach
sections.line: A technical publisher asked to license One Human, Nine Agents, Nineteen Hours; answer for the landscape, not one.

sections.label: Who takes books like this
sections.line: Pragmatic from 42%, No Starch's menu and its all-rights contract, others say only competitive or nothing.

sections.label: It has been done before
sections.line: Clojure for the Brave and True, Understanding ECMAScript 6, Lumen, Think Python, Eloquent JavaScript.

sections.label: Where Leanpub stands
sections.line: The author keeps the copyright; Leanpub's licence is non-exclusive; ask for the ebook to be carved out.

sections.label: The questions to ask
sections.line: License not assign, the Leanpub edition, term and reversion, royalties, translation and audio, non-compete, title, licence.

sections.label: Other routes for the same book

sections.label: What I want to keep
sections.line: A licence, not a sale: the publisher widens the audience, the Leanpub edition stays open and updated.
